To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the VAX ratio is a useful measure of the intensity with which a country participates in production sharing and that bilateral production sharing is important for understanding the value added content in bilateral trade.
1) the VAX ratio varies widely across countries and sectors, and 2) it is a measure of both the intensity of production chains, and the degree to which production chains are triangular.

(1) the value added content is a useful measure to analyze the structure and the dynamics of trade, (2) the value added share in gross exports is a good indicator of the degree of production sharing in the economy, and (3) the bilateral value added content in gross exports provides a good measure of the bilateral trade linkages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement and analysis of international trade in intermediate goods.
understanding how production sharing and the international fragmentation of production are affecting international trade.
the role of intermediate inputs in international trade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the value added content in bilateral trade varies widely and contains information on both bilateral as well as triangular production chains.
the VAX ratio, as a measure of production sharing, is an important indicator of bilateral trade linkages, but it should not be confused with the value added content in gross trade flows.
production sharing and trade in intermediates are important phenomena, which are not well understood and deserve further study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
production sharing is a pervasive feature of global production and trade.
the VAX ratio is a good indicator of production sharing, but it should not be interpreted in isolation.
the VAX ratio measures bilateral production linkages and that these linkages differ across countries, sectors, and partners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
value added data can be used to study the role of production sharing in international trade.
value added trade data provide a more complete picture of international trade than gross trade data.
production sharing, as measured by VAX ratios, is an important component of bilateral trade and should be taken into account in trade policy analysis and trade agreements.
